spans.s:
गभस्तल गभस्तल, अम्, n., N. of a hell;
[cf. गभस्ति-मत्.]

गभस्ति गभस्ति, इस्, इस्, m. f. (related to
गभ; the original meaning may have been a fork),
Ved. a particular part of a carriage, the shaft; the
double-edged thunderbolt of Indra (?); the fore part
of the arm, the hand; a ray of light, a sun-beam, a
moon-beam, i. e. the hands of the sun or moon;
(इस्), m. the sun; (इस्), f. an epithet of Svāhā, the
wife of Agni.
—गभस्ति-नेमि, इस्, m. an epithet of
Kṛṣṇa.
—गभस्ति-पाणि, इस्, m. the sun, ‘having
rays for hands.’
—गभस्ति-पूत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved.
purified with the hands.
—गभस्ति-मत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, shining, brilliant; (आन्), m. the sun; N. of one
of the nine divisions of Bhārata-varṣa; (अत्), n. one
of the seven divisions of Pātāla or the region below
the earth.
—गभस्ति-हस्त, अस्, m. the sun; [cf.
गभस्ति-पाणि.]

गभिषक् गभि-षक्, ind. (fr. गभि, related
to गभ and सज् fr. rt. सञ्ज्), Ved. deeply down,
far down or within; [cf. आनुषक्.]

गभीका गभीका, f., N. of a plant and its
fruit.

गभीर गभीर or गम्भीर, अस्, आ, अम् (re-
lated to गभ and गभस्ति, ‘a deep cleft;’ the Ṛg-
veda generally uses गभीर and only गम्भीर at
the beginning of a Pāda or quarter-verse; in post-Vedic
writings गम्भीर is the more usual form, but
गभीर occurs occasionally even in the latest writers),
deep (opposed to गाध and दीन); deep in sound,
deep-sounding, hollow in sound, hollow-toned (there-
fore enumerated in the Nighaṇṭu among the synonyms
of वाच्); profound, sagacious, grave, serious, solemn,
earnest, secret, mysterious; dense, impervious; not
to be penetrated, not to be investigated or explored,
inscrutable, difficult to be perceived or understood;
inexhaustible, continuous, uninterrupted (as time &c.).
The deepness of a man's navel, of his voice, and of his
character are sometimes praised together: when a
man is said to have a deep navel, voice and character,
he is said to be त्रि-गम्भीरः; (अस्), m. (without
the nasal), N. of a descendant of Āyu; (with the
nasal), the lemon tree [cf. जम्भीर and जम्बीर];
a lotus; a Mantra of the Ṛg-veda: (आ), f. hiccup,
violent singultus; N. of a river; गभीर, अम्, n.
depth; [cf. Lith. gillybe, gelme, gyle; gillus: Slav.
glûbok; glûbina.]
—गम्भीर-चेतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्,
Ved. of profound mind.
—गम्भीर-ता, f. or गम्-
भीर-त्व, अम्, n. depth (of water); depth of sound;
profoundness, earnestness, sagacity.
—गम्भीर-
ध्वनि, इस्, m. a deep sound, low note or tone.
—गम्भीर-नाद or गभीर-शब्द, अस्, m. a
deep or hollow sound, thundering, roaring
—गम्-
भीर-निर्घोष, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga
—गम्-
भीर-वेदिन्, ई, इनी, इ lit. deeply sagacious, restive
(as an elephant).
—गम्भीर-वेध, अस्, आ, अम्,
very penetrating.
—गम्भीर-वेपस् or गभीर-
वेपस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. moved deeply or inwardly,
deeply excited.
—गम्भीर-शंस, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved.
ruling secretly or in a hidden manner; (Sāy.) whose
praise is inexhaustible, an epithet of Varuṇa.
—गम्-
भीर-सत्त्व-स्वर-नाभि, इस्, इस्, इ, having a deep
character, voice, and navel.
—गम्भीर-स्वामिन्, ई,
m. the inscrutable lord; N. of a figure representing
Nārāyaṇa.
—गम्भीरार्थ (˚र-अर्˚), अस्, m. pro-
found sense or meaning.

गभीरिका, f. a large drum with a deep sound; a
gong; [cf. गम्भीरक.]

गभोलिक गभोलिक, अस्, m. a small round
pillow, = मसूर.
